## devonthink
CRITICAL — Database package safety: DEVONthink databases are stored as packages (.dtBase2) or sparse images (.dtSparse, .dtArchive). Never modify, rename, move, or delete files inside a database package directly via the filesystem. All record and content operations must go through this MCP server or, as a fallback, via AppleScript. Direct filesystem manipulation will corrupt the database and cause irreversible data loss.

Batch operations: Use the uuids array parameter instead of sequential single-record calls for tag, update, move, trash, duplicate, replicate, and export operations. Batch mode is faster, reduces round trips, and returns a summary with succeeded/failed counts.

Avoiding duplicates: Use lookup_records (by name, URL, path, filename, or comment) before create_record to check whether a record already exists.

Content editing: Prefer update_record_content with mode append or insert over replace for large documents. Replace mode requires sending the entire new content and risks accidental data loss if the content is incomplete.

Group hierarchies: Use create_group_path to create nested group structures in a single call (like mkdir -p) rather than sequential create_record calls.

AI-powered tools: classify_record and find_similar_records use DEVONthink's built-in AI algorithms and proprietary training data — they provide organizational suggestions that complement, not duplicate, your own capabilities.

Record enrichment: resolve_doi_metadata and resolve_book_metadata can enrich existing records with bibliographic metadata by passing the record's uuid — there is no need to create a new record.

AI exclusion: Records marked as excluded from AI access (excludeFromChat) are protected in two ways. (1) Input protection: any tool that receives such a record's UUID as an argument refuses to operate on it and returns an error. (2) Output protection: result lists from tools like search_records, classify_record, find_similar_records, get_record_children, get_record_duplicates, and the link traversal tools are filt… [truncated]

2	
3	A catalogue of refactoring opportunities in the **production** code, each mapped to a
4	[Fowler code smell](https://agilepainrelief.com/glossary/code-smells/). **Every catalogued
5	item (RF-01→13, RV-01→11, RF-09 residue) is now done** — this is kept as a _record_, not a
6	live to-do list.
7	
8	## Status — 2026-07-08 (catalogue complete)
9	
10	All catalogued refactorings are **closed**: Tier 1 (RF-01→03), Tier 2 (RF-04→07),
11	Tier 3 (RF-08→11), Tier 4 (RF-12→13), and every code-review follow-up (RV-01→11).
12	`svelte-check` is at **0 errors / 0 warnings** (the separate type-check-cleanup PRD also
13	landed). The deferred **RF-D1/RF-D2** value-object questions are **decided: keep
14	primitives** (RF-D1 flagged as the likeliest future adopt, with a revisit trigger).
15	
16	**Only non-code item left:** the deferred **test-suite** cleanup pass (see _Not yet
17	catalogued_) — by agreement a separate later effort.
18	
19	### Going forward (doc role)
20	
21	- **This file is a reference/record, not a working backlog.** Per the single-working-list
22	  rule, _new_ refactoring ideas start as one-liners in [`product-backlog.md`](product-backlog.md);
23	  promote one to a detailed `RF-NN` / `RV-NN` entry here only when work actually starts,
24	  so this doc never grows a parallel open list.
25	- **Ordering:** the numbered catalogue below stays in tier order (append the next free
26	  `RF-NN` at the end of its tier — numbers are stable ids, don't renumber). Dated status
27	  notes like this one go **newest at the top**.
28	- Completed entries keep their **Landed** notes — they document the non-obvious
29	  behaviour-preservation calls, which is the main reason to keep the file rather than
30	  delete it.
31	
32	## How this is ranked
33	
34	- **Tier = blast radius** (change amplification): how many files you must touch
35	  today to make one routine change. Headline → High → Medium → Low.
36	- **Correctness-risk items are hoisted** above pure tidiness at the same tier.
37	- Each entry tags the **smell**, a rough **effort** (S / M / L), and lists
38	  **sibling sites** rather than repeating the entry per location.
39	- **Out of scope (already decided, not "missed"):** image lazy-loading, signed-URL
40	  batching, and the deliberate deferral of pagination — see
41	  [ADR 0001](adr/0001-list-performance-attack-image-loading-not-pagination.md) and
42	  [ADR 0002](adr/0002-batch-receipt-signed-urls.md). Where a smell touches one of
43	  those decisions, it is cross-referenced, not re-litigated.
44	
45	## Coding preferences applied
46	
47	- **Guard clauses / early returns are good** — fixes that flatten nesting via early
48	  return are encouraged, never flagged.
49	- **Heterogeneous union return types** (`string | number | object`) are a violation;
50	  a _well-formed_ discriminated union (see `validateFile()` below) is the model to
51	  copy.
52	- **`any` is a smell wherever a more precise type exists** — prefer `unknown` +
53	  narrowing, typed rows, typed DTOs. Leave `any` only where the library gives no
54	  usable type, and say so.
55	- **Forced-upstream `T | null`** (provider-imposed nullability) is flagged at low
56	  priority only.
57	
58	---
59	
60	## Code-review findings — 2026-07-05 (post RF-04→RF-13 sweep)
61	
62	A `/code-review` pass over the uncommitted RF-04→RF-13 working tree. The refactor
63	was **behavior-preserving** on every correctness-sensitive path (CSV sign
64	conventions, matching tolerances, reconciliation scoring/sort, the no-orphan-storage
65	guarantee) — no correctness regressions. What it surfaced is one incomplete
66	extraction plus a cluster of altitude / efficiency / typing residue. **RV-01…RV-05
67	were fixed in that same working tree; RV-06…RV-11 were the softer items deferred then —
68	all now closed (see each entry's Landed note).**
69	
70	### Fixed
71	
72	- [x] **RV-01 — Reconciliation left out of the RF-09 category-resolver migration.**
73	      `reconciliation/+page.svelte:loadCategories()` still hand-rolled the
74	      `categories.find(...)` loop that `buildCategoryMap()` replaced (the receipts page
75	      migrated; reconciliation was missed, despite `resolveCategory.ts`'s doc claiming
76	      both). The loop also lacked the denormalized `category_name`/`category_color`
77	      fallback, so a receipt whose `category_id` wasn't in the freshly-loaded family list
78	      rendered as uncategorized in the reconciliation edit-modal swatch but resolved on
79	      the receipts page. **Fix:** delegate to `buildCategoryMap(expenses, categories)`.
80	- [x] **RV-02 — FC confidence bands frozen while the tolerance is configurable.**
81	      `MatchingTolerances` exposed `foreignCurrencyTolerancePercent` as a field, but the
82	      `0.02` / `0.03` confidence bands stayed hardcoded module constants — widening the
83	      tolerance would pass wider pairs through the gate yet score them all `near/low`.
84	      **Fix:** moved both bands into `MatchingTolerances`
85	      (`foreignCurrencyHighConfidencePercent` / `…MediumConfidencePercent`, defaults
86	      `0.02` / `0.03`) so they travel with the tolerance. Behavior unchanged at defaults.
87	- [x] **RV-03 — `PDFExportService.drawImageUnavailable(wrap)` flag froze an
88	      accidental divergence.** The "image fetch returned null" path passed `wrap=false`
89	      (no word-wrap) while the missing-path and error paths wrapped — a long merchant
90	      name overflowed the page margin in one of three identical-message paths. **Fix:**
91	      dropped the flag; the helper always wraps.
92	- [x] **RV-04 — Per-row `resolveCategory()` `Array.find` on the expenses table.**
93	      `expenses/+page.svelte` called `resolveCategory(expense, categories)` inside the
94	      `categoryCell` snippet — O(rows × categories) on every reactive re-render.
95	      **Fix:** compute a `$derived` `buildCategoryMap(expenses, categories)` once and do
96	      an O(1) lookup per row.
97	- [x] **RV-05 — Redundant `as Category[]` cast** on
98	      `getFamilyCategories()` in `reconciliation/+page.svelte` (already returns
99	      `Category[]`; the receipts page dropped the identical cast). **Fix:** removed.
100	
101	### Follow-ups (softer / lower-confidence — deferred at the sweep, all now closed)
102	
103	- [x] **RV-06 — `Expense` / `ExpenseReceiptRow` typed `total_amount` as non-null**
104	      while `receipts.total_amount` is nullable (`001_init.sql`, and `ReconciliationService`
105	      guards `.not('total_amount','is',null)`). The lie let two exporters fake a zero:
106	      `CSVExportService.formatAmount` emitted `0.00` and `PDFExportService.formatAmount`
107	      returned `$0.00` for an OCR-unread amount. **Landed (blank + flag):** widened both
108	      types to `number | null`; CSV export now leaves the amount field blank and PDF
109	      renders `—`; the expenses/receipts amount cells show a `⚠ Amount not read` badge
110	      (mirroring the duplicate/suspicious-date badges) instead of a misleading value; the
111	      expenses sort uses `?? 0`. Decision: amountless receipts are **shown and flagged**,
112	      never hidden or zeroed. New unit tests cover CSV-blank, PDF-em-dash, and
113	      `getExpenses` carrying null through; existing `$0.00`-for-null assertions repointed.
114	- [x] **RV-07 — `buildCategoryMap()` writes an explicit `null`** for uncategorized
115	      receipts where the old receipts-page loop left the key **absent**
116	      (`receipts/+page.svelte:255`). **Verified no-op:** the only consumer reads
117	      `categoryMap[editingReceipt.id] ?? null` (line ~940) — a nullish read, not a
118	      key-presence check (`in` / `Object.keys().length`), so the null-vs-absent
119	      distinction is invisible. No change needed.
120	- [x] **RV-08 — Scattered `as unknown as` join-shape casts in `ExpenseService`**
121	      (was `:~104`, `:~324`). **Landed:** consolidated into one named, documented boundary
122	      `coerceEmbed<T>(value: unknown): T` (module-private in `ExpenseService`) that explains
123	      the PostgREST to-one-embed-typed-as-array coercion once; both call sites now read
124	      `coerceEmbed<ExpenseReceiptRow[]>(…)` / `coerceEmbed<{ name: string } | null>(…)` with
125	      no inline `as unknown as` and no duplicated comment. `svelte-check` clean; 97
126	      ExpenseService tests green.
127	- [x] **RV-09 — `PDFExportService` sub-methods share a single mutable `PageCursor`.**
128	      **Landed:** promoted `PageCursor` from a bare mutable interface to a small class that
129	      owns page advancement — `PageCursor.start(pdfDoc)` + `cursor.ensureRoom(minY)`. Page
130	      swapping is now the cursor's own responsibility (drawing helpers only read `page` /
131	      move `y`, never swap the page), and `pdfDoc` is no longer threaded through
132	      `drawCategoryTable` / `drawGrandTotal` / `ensureRoom` (Data Clump also removed). The
133	      old free `startPage`/`ensureRoom` methods are gone. Behaviour-preserving; the 33
134	      `generateReceiptPDF` tests (the only surface exercised) stay green.
135	- [x] **RV-10 — `ReceiptService.computeRemainingAmount` is named as a pure compute
136	      but validates and throws.** **Landed:** renamed to `validateAndComputeRemaining` — an
137	      honest name for the third split-validation step (after `validateSplitAmount` /
138	      `validateSplitDate`). Doc notes it runs post-fetch because it needs the original's
139	      total, and returns the remainder it validates. Kept together deliberately: the
140	      total-relative rule (`remainingAmount <= 0` after cent-rounding) can't be separated
141	      from the compute without a double-compute. 99 ReceiptService/split tests green.
142	- [x] **RV-11 — Dead re-check in `ReconciliationService.scoreCandidate`** (`:~373`):
143	      after the `if (isForeignCurrency && !receipt.exchange_rate_to_cad) return null`
144	      guard, the CAD-amount ternary re-tested `isForeignCurrency && receipt.exchange_rate_to_cad`
145	      — required only because the `!` guard shape defeated TS narrowing. **Landed:** merged
146	      the guard and the conversion into a single `if (isForeignCurrency) { … }` block so
147	      `exchange_rate_to_cad` narrows to non-null after the inner guard — no double condition
148	      and no non-null assertion. Behaviour-preserving; matching tests green.
149	
150	---

152	## Tier 1 — Headline (highest change amplification)
153	
154	### RF-01 — CSV parsers duplicate the whole parse loop (Template Method gap)
155	
156	- [x] **Smell:** Duplicated Code + Conditional Complexity · **Effort:** M · **Done**
157	- **Where:** `src/lib/services/csvParsers/AmexParser.ts`,
158	  `EQBankParser.ts`, `PCFinancialParser.ts`, `RBCFinancialParser.ts`,
159	  `SimpliiFinancialParser.ts`, `TDBankParser.ts`, `WealthSimpleParser.ts`
160	- **Evidence:** Every parser's `parse()` repeats the identical skeleton —
161	  `removeBOM()` → `parseCSV()` → locate header → resolve column indices → row
162	  loop → `parseDate()` / `parseAmount()` / `normalizeAmount()` → validate
163	  description → `push()` → collect errors. Compare `AmexParser.ts:10-100` with
164	  `EQBankParser.ts:10-88`: structurally the same, differing only in (a) header
165	  detection, (b) column-name matching, and (c) the `invertSign` flag. `BaseCSVParser`
166	  supplies the _utilities_ but never a `parse()` **template**, so each subclass
167	  re-implements the orchestration.
168	- **Fix:** Pull the orchestration into `BaseCSVParser` as a Template Method and let
169	  subclasses override only the parts that actually vary:
170	
171	  ```ts
172	  // BaseCSVParser
173	  parse(csvContent: string): CSVParseResult {
174	    const transactions: ParsedTransaction[] = [];
175	    const errors: string[] = [];
176	    const rows = this.parseCSV(this.removeBOM(csvContent));
177	    if (rows.length < 2) { errors.push('CSV file is empty or has no data rows'); return { transactions, errors }; }
178	
179	    const header = this.findHeaderRow(rows);          // hook
180	    if (!header) { errors.push(this.formatError()); return { transactions, errors }; }
181	
182	    for (let i = header.dataStart; i < rows.length; i++) {
183	      const parsed = this.parseRow(rows[i], header.columns, i, errors); // hook
184	      if (parsed) transactions.push(parsed);
185	    }
186	    return { transactions, errors };
187	  }
188	  protected abstract findHeaderRow(rows: string[][]): HeaderInfo | null;
189	  protected abstract parseRow(row: string[], cols: ColumnIndex, i: number, errors: string[]): ParsedTransaction | null;
190	  ```
191	
192	  This removes ~400 lines of copy-paste and makes a new bank a ~20-line subclass.
193	
194	- **Note:** Keep the per-bank sign conventions intact — see the `invertSign` /
195	  Wealth Simple `type`-column rules in `CLAUDE.md`; this is correctness-sensitive.
196	- **Landed:** `BaseCSVParser.parse()` is now the shared Template Method (BOM →
197	  `parseCSV` → empty-file guard → `resolveLayout()` hook → row loop → single
198	  `try/catch`). Subclasses override only `resolveLayout()` (header/column matching)
199	  and `parseRow()`; the single-amount banks share `finalizeRow()`, which
200	  consolidates the `normalizeAmount` → assignment step. Side effects that fell out
201	  of the consolidation:
202	  - Cleared the **6 production type errors** (`normalizeAmount`'s `number | null`
203	    flowing into `amount: number`) — `finalizeRow` guards the null and returns a
204	    plain `number`. `npm run check` drops 118 → 112 (the RF-01-owned slice of the

# Refactoring backlog — completed record

A catalogue of refactoring opportunities in the **production** code, each mapped to a
[Fowler code smell](https://agilepainrelief.com/glossary/code-smells/). **Every catalogued
item (RF-01→13, RV-01→11, RF-09 residue) is now done** — this is kept as a _record_, not a
live to-do list.

## Status — 2026-07-08 (catalogue complete)

All catalogued refactorings are **closed**: Tier 1 (RF-01→03), Tier 2 (RF-04→07),
Tier 3 (RF-08→11), Tier 4 (RF-12→13), and every code-review follow-up (RV-01→11).
`svelte-check` is at **0 errors / 0 warnings** (the separate type-check-cleanup PRD also
landed). The deferred **RF-D1/RF-D2** value-object questions are **decided: keep
primitives** (RF-D1 flagged as the likeliest future adopt, with a revisit trigger).

**Only non-code item left:** the deferred **test-suite** cleanup pass (see _Not yet
catalogued_) — by agreement a separate later effort.

### Going forward (doc role)

- **This file is a reference/record, not a working backlog.** Per the single-working-list
  rule, _new_ refactoring ideas start as one-liners in [`product-backlog.md`](product-backlog.md);
  promote one to a detailed `RF-NN` / `RV-NN` entry here only when work actually starts,
  so this doc never grows a parallel open list.
- **Ordering:** the numbered catalogue below stays in tier order (append the next free
  `RF-NN` at the end of its tier — numbers are stable ids, don't renumber). Dated status
  notes like this one go **newest at the top**.
- Completed entries keep their **Landed** notes — they document the non-obvious
  behaviour-preservation calls, which is the main reason to keep the file rather than
  delete it.

## How this is ranked

- **Tier = blast radius** (change amplification): how many files you must touch
  today to make one routine change. Headline → High → Medium → Low.
- **Correctness-risk items are hoisted** above pure tidiness at the same tier.
- Each entry tags the **smell**, a rough **effort** (S / M / L), and lists
  **sibling sites** rather than repeating the entry per location.
- **Out of scope (already decided, not "missed"):** image lazy-loading, signed-URL
  batching, and the deliberate deferral of pagination — see
  [ADR 0001](adr/0001-list-performance-attack-image-loading-not-pagination.md) and
  [ADR 0002](adr/0002-batch-receipt-signed-urls.md). Where a smell touches one of
  those decisions, it is cross-referenced, not re-litigated.

## Coding preferences applied

- **Guard clauses / early returns are good** — fixes that flatten nesting via early
  return are encouraged, never flagged.
- **Heterogeneous union return types** (`string | number | object`) are a violation;
  a _well-formed_ discriminated union (see `validateFile()` below) is the model to
  copy.
- **`any` is a smell wherever a more precise type exists** — prefer `unknown` +
  narrowing, typed rows, typed DTOs. Leave `any` only where the library gives no
  usable type, and say so.
- **Forced-upstream `T | null`** (provider-imposed nullability) is flagged at low
  priority only.

---

## Code-review findings — 2026-07-05 (post RF-04→RF-13 sweep)

A `/code-review` pass over the uncommitted RF-04→RF-13 working tree. The refactor
was **behavior-preserving** on every correctness-sensitive path (CSV sign
conventions, matching tolerances, reconciliation scoring/sort, the no-orphan-storage

### RF-01 — CSV parsers duplicate the whole parse loop (Template Method gap)

- [x] **Smell:** Duplicated Code + Conditional Complexity · **Effort:** M · **Done**
- **Where:** `src/lib/services/csvParsers/AmexParser.ts`,
  `EQBankParser.ts`, `PCFinancialParser.ts`, `RBCFinancialParser.ts`,
  `SimpliiFinancialParser.ts`, `TDBankParser.ts`, `WealthSimpleParser.ts`
- **Evidence:** Every parser's `parse()` repeats the identical skeleton —
  `removeBOM()` → `parseCSV()` → locate header → resolve column indices → row
  loop → `parseDate()` / `parseAmount()` / `normalizeAmount()` → validate
  description → `push()` → collect errors. Compare `AmexParser.ts:10-100` with
  `EQBankParser.ts:10-88`: structurally the same, differing only in (a) header
  detection, (b) column-name matching, and (c) the `invertSign` flag. `BaseCSVParser`
  supplies the _utilities_ but never a `parse()` **template**, so each subclass
  re-implements the orchestration.
- **Fix:** Pull the orchestration into `BaseCSVParser` as a Template Method and let
  subclasses override only the parts that actually vary:

  ```ts
  // BaseCSVParser
  parse(csvContent: string): CSVParseResult {
    const transactions: ParsedTransaction[] = [];
    const errors: string[] = [];
    const rows = this.parseCSV(this.removeBOM(csvContent));
    if (rows.length < 2) { errors.push('CSV file is empty or has no data rows'); return { transactions, errors }; }

    const header = this.findHeaderRow(rows);          // hook
    if (!header) { errors.push(this.formatError()); return { transactions, errors }; }

    for (let i = header.dataStart; i < rows.length; i++) {
      const parsed = this.parseRow(rows[i], header.columns, i, errors); // hook
      if (parsed) transactions.push(parsed);
    }
    return { transactions, errors };
  }
  protected abstract findHeaderRow(rows: string[][]): HeaderInfo | null;
  protected abstract parseRow(row: string[], cols: ColumnIndex, i: number, errors: string[]): ParsedTransaction | null;
  ```

  This removes ~400 lines of copy-paste and makes a new bank a ~20-line subclass.

- **Note:** Keep the per-bank sign conventions intact — see the `invertSign` /
  Wealth Simple `type`-column rules in `CLAUDE.md`; this is correctness-sensitive.
- **Landed:** `BaseCSVParser.parse()` is now the shared Template Method (BOM →
  `parseCSV` → empty-file guard → `resolveLayout()` hook → row loop → single
  `try/catch`). Subclasses override only `resolveLayout()` (header/column matching)
  and `parseRow()`; the single-amount banks share `finalizeRow()`, which
  consolidates the `normalizeAmount` → assignment step. Side effects that fell out
  of the consolidation:
  - Cleared the **6 production type errors** (`normalizeAmount`'s `number | null`
    flowing into `amount: number`) — `finalizeRow` guards the null and returns a
    plain `number`. `npm run check` drops 118 → 112 (the RF-01-owned slice of the
    [type-check-cleanup PRD](prd-type-check-cleanup.md); the remaining 112 are that
    PRD's, so "0 errors" only lands once **both** are done).
  - Fixed the **Wealth Simple missing-`try/catch`** inconsistency: WS now runs
    through the shared template (with `minimumRowCount = 0` to preserve its
    header-only-is-valid behaviour), so all seven parsers are wrapped once.
  - Removed all six parser `catch (e: any)` sites (they collapse into the base
    `catch (e: unknown)`), partially clearing **RF-08**.
  - `normalizeAmount`'s `(amount, invertSign)` signature is unchanged (its direct

scheduled. Kept here as recorded decisions, not open questions. RF-D1 is the more
likely eventual payoff; RF-D2 is a firmer won't-do.

- **Status:** Deferred — **keep bare `number` + `currency` for now; likeliest future adopt.**
- **Smell:** Primitive Obsession + Data Clump
- **Where:** `total_amount` / `currency` / `exchange_rate_to_cad` travel as a loose

  `formatCurrencyWithEstimate` call sites on expenses / reconciliation.
- **Trade-off:** A `Money` type is the textbook fix and would localise sign/rounding
  risk — **but introducing it touches every parser, service, and page**. For a family
  expense app that may be over-engineering _today_.

  sign/rounding/FC-conversion risk it localises is exactly the class the CSV
  `invertSign` rules and the reconciliation scoring keep circling.

- **Status:** Deferred — **keep the string + helper convention (firm won't-do).**

  regressing correctness that's already hardened. Only reconsider if a date type-safety
  bug (not a timezone bug) actually bites.

Net: ~82 hollow reimplementation tests replaced by real coverage. Both teeth-proven. **Third offender (later found):** `ReceiptImageViewer.spec.ts` (859 lines) was the worst of the lot — every `it()` re-declared the zoom arithmetic _inline_ (`let zoom = 100; zoom += 50; expect(zoom).toBe(150)`) and asserted against its own copy, never rendering the component (its header admitted it was stale TDD RED-phase scaffolding). Teeth-proven. Non-finds: `ReceiptService.bulk.spec.ts`'s `expect.fail` are legit "should have thrown" guards. `family-category-visibility.spec.ts` — **decision made: KEEP.** It's an env-gated (`describeIf(SUPABASE_URL && SERVICE_KEY)`) RLS integration suite — never runs in CI, but it's the _only_ executable check of the family-scoping row-level-security policies the migrations define (removed members can't see data, unique constraints), which unit tests can't cover. Each was proven with an induced production break. The `#{#ath1c}` no-per-page-redirect guard remains a source check in `auth-route-guard.spec.ts` (a page-level absence-of-anti-pattern, orthogonal to the layout render).

failure, one spec file per PR-sized unit — see `.scratch/handoff-test-suite-cleanup.md`.

- **Convert source-introspection specs → behavior tests. ✅ DONE.** All 10 `readFileSync`-their-own-source specs were converted to real behavior tests (render via the `*.svelte.spec.ts` harness or exercise the service/util directly) or deleted as redundant. The only surviving source check is `auth-route-guard.spec.ts`'s `#{#ath1c}` no-per-page-redirect guard, kept deliberately (see the render-harness item below). Converting them surfaced a real false-positive bug-in-a-test (Profile link "visible to all users") and confirmed several bodies of logic were already covered by util/service specs.
- **Split oversized service specs. ✅ DONE (3 of 4; the 4th is single-concern).** Each split preserved the exact test set (oracle: identical passing count before/after).
  - `ExpenseService.spec.ts` (2165) → `ExpenseService.{getExpenses,categoryAssignment,vendorRules,matchStatus}.spec.ts` + shared `expenseServiceTestHelpers.ts` (105 tests).
  - `expenses-page-filters.spec.ts` (1404) → `expenses-filters.{uncategorized,categoryAnalytics,dateFilter,filterCount}.spec.ts` + shared `builders/expenseFilterFixtures.ts` (85 tests). _(These four were subsequently deleted/converted — the tests turned out to be reimplemented-logic; see the reimplemented-logic bullet below.)_
  - `ReceiptService.spec.ts` (1276) → `ReceiptService.{suspiciousDate,autoCategory,uploadMeta}.spec.ts` (44 tests). The `vi.mock` preamble is replicated per file (hoisting can't be shared via import).
  - `ReceiptService.split.spec.ts` (1024) — **left intact**: it is a single cohesive concern (the receipt-split feature) with a shared module-level `beforeEach`; concern-splitting a single-concern spec adds duplication for little gain.
- **Route inline row-building through the builders. ✅ DONE (small footprint).** `duplicateDetection.spec.ts`'s local `createReceipt` factory now delegates to `makeReceiptRow` (dropping an `as ReceiptRow` cast; oracle: 19 tests unchanged). Audit finding: most other "inline rows" are NOT builder candidates — they're partial Supabase query-result shapes (`ExpenseService.matchStatus`, `ReceiptService.autoCategory/uploadMeta` — the DB returns a subset of columns, not a full `ReceiptRow`), deliberate single-field minimal stubs (`reconciliationRowEdit.spec.ts`), or dead code (`duplicateHelpers.spec.ts`'s unused `createReceipt`). Forcing the builder into those would mis-shape the mock or add noise.
- **Foreign-currency amount cell render test. ✅ DONE.** The inline `total_amount * exchange_rate_to_cad` CAD-estimate math in the `amountCell` snippets of both `expenses/+page.svelte` and `receipts/+page.svelte` now has behavior coverage on the render harness: `expenses-page.svelte.spec.ts` and `receipts-page.svelte.spec.ts` render a foreign-currency (EUR, rate 1.53) row and assert `€45.00 (≈$68.85)`, plus a null-rate case that shows no estimate. Both production math sites were teeth-proven (turning `*` into `+` broke the estimate). No production extraction was needed after all — the harness made it directly testable.
- **Convert reimplemented-logic specs → real behavior/util tests. ✅ DONE.** The four `expenses-filters.*` specs tested locally-defined copies of the page's filter/analytics logic (`filterByCategory`, `calculateSpendingSummary`, `filterExpensesByURLDates`, …) — green whether or not the real code works. Net: ~82 hollow reimplementation tests replaced by real coverage. Also fixed a pre-existing `as any` in `dateValidation.spec.ts`. **Second-frontier sweep (follow-up):** two more offenders found and converted — (1) `CategoryDropdown.spec.ts` re-declared ~25 copies of the component's filter/validate/keyboard logic → replaced by a real render test `CategoryDropdown.svelte.spec.ts`, which **surfaced a production bug**: clicking "Create new category…" closed the whole dropdown (Svelte 5 flushes state synchronously after the delegated click handler, so the create button detaches before the document click-outside listener runs, which then treats the detached target as an outside click) — fixed in `CategoryDropdown.svelte` with an `isConnected` guard; (2) `transactions-page-filters.spec.ts` re-declared the page's `applyClientFilters`/`hasActiveFilters` → extracted the real predicate to `src/lib/utils/transactionFilters.ts` (page delegates), tested in `transactionFilters.spec.ts`. - **Route/layout render harness — BUILT & USED.** `src/lib/tests/harness/appMocks.ts` (+ `LayoutHarness.svelte`) mocks the SvelteKit + Supabase module boundaries and exposes controllable state: `setRoute`/`setSession`/`setSessionPending`, `setReceipts`/`setExpenses`/`setCategories`/`setProfile`, and `ReceiptServiceStub`/`ExpenseServiceStub`/`CategoryServiceStub`. It renders real `+layout.svelte` / `+page.svelte` / components in the `client` project. Every page/layout/component introspection spec was converted on it: `layout-render.svelte.spec.ts` (layout gate + nav, was auth-route-guard + layout-navigation), `receipt-image-click.svelte.spec.ts`, `expenses-page.svelte.spec.ts`, `receipts-page.svelte.spec.ts` (filter wiring), `expenses-page-receipt-modal.svelte.spec.ts` (row → modal), `profile-page.svelte.spec.ts`, and `ReceiptEditModal.svelte.spec.ts` (component: validation/discard/notice/category/filename). Both slices done and verified. Here's the summary.

## 1. Shared `fetchMock.ts` fixture ✅

New `src/lib/tests/fixtures/fetchMock.ts` exporting:
- `stubFetchJson(body, { ok, status })` — sets `globalThis.fetch` to a mock resolving JSON, returns the mock for assertions
- `stubFetchReject(error)` — network-error path
- `installFetchMock()` — saves current fetch, returns a `restore()` for `afterEach`

**Migrated:** `ExchangeRateService.spec.ts` (save/restore lifecycle + 8 inline `{ok, json}` stubs collapsed to helpers — the Bank-of-Canada `observations` payload stays visible per test) and the `ReceiptService.autoCategory`/`uploadMeta` `mockOcr` helpers + reject stubs.

**Scope correction I made:** the original estimate over-counted. `imageResize` and `receiptDateCorrection` don't actually mock `fetch`, and `PDFExportService`'s `fetchImageFn` is an *injected callback* (DI), not global fetch — so none of those were touched. Real consumers were 3 files.

## 2. `makeCategory` builder + inline-literal migration ✅

Added `makeCategory(overrides): Category` to `rowBuilders.ts` and migrated the **genuine** repeated `Category` domain-object sites: `resolveCategory`, `expenses-page`, `ReceiptEditModal`, `CategoryDropdown`, `PDFExportService` — removing **five `as Category` casts** and an unused import.

**Scoped out after inspection** (and documented why in the backlog — this matches the repo's earlier "inline rows are partial query shapes" finding):
- **No `makeVendorCategoryRule`** — vendor-rule literals are 2-field partial query results, not full rows.
- **CategoryService.spec's** `categories` literals are partial/legacy-`user_id` raw DB-result shapes → stay inline.
- **family-category-visibility** uses `.insert({...})` payloads to a real DB → not builder shapes.
- **`ReconciliationService`/`categoryAssignment`** build no Category objects (the earlier agent list was over-broad; `category_id` strings are just method args).
- **No `makeSplitReceiptRow`** — `ReceiptService.split.spec.ts` already delegates to `makeReceiptRow`, so its 1024 lines are inherent test scenarios, not fixture duplication. Nothing to shrink there.

## Verification
- Full unit suite green: **1240 passed, 8 skipped** (unchanged)
- `svelte-check`: **0 errors / 0 warnings**

content.text:
Done. The dead-tag and stale-header sweep is complete and fully verified.

## What changed

**Dead `#{#…}` spec tags — all 314 removed across 40 spec files.** From JSDoc headers, `describe`/`it` labels, and inline comments. Prose was preserved throughout — e.g. `Data integrity (atomic operations)` and `(URL Parameter Validation)` kept; only the tag tokens went.

**Stale TDD-RED ceremony — removed.** `Specifications covered:`, `Authority:`, `Priority:`, `Traceable to:`, `Specification: specs/…` header lines, plus differently-worded stragglers my main pass didn't catch and I hand-fixed: `TDD RED PHASE` (pdfDetection), `RED PHASE … does not exist yet` (sharedDateFilter — reworded to present tense since RF-02 shipped the module), the dead spec-path header (passwordValidation), and a stale `// RED PHASE TEST` comment (ReconciliationService).

**Deliberately kept:** `ReceiptImageViewer.svelte.spec.ts`'s header, which *describes* the old hollow spec as "stale TDD RED-phase scaffolding" — that's meaningful history, not a live tag.

## How I did it safely

A token-first transform (parenthetical tag-groups → bare tag-runs → light label/space cleanup), **guarded to only touch tag-bearing lines** so executable code was provably untouched. I caught two bugs in dry-runs before applying: an early version ate `vi.fn()` → `vi.fn` and `() =>` → `=>`; the final version preserved those exactly (verified `vi.fn()` 21→21, `() =>` 61→61 in the heaviest file). A multi-line paren in ReceiptEditModal, six trailing-space labels, and dangling blank comment lines were hand-fixed after.

## Verification

- Full unit suite: **1240 passed, 8 skipped** — unchanged, nothing broke
- `svelte-check`: **0 errors / 0 warnings**
- ESLint: clean; Prettier applied to all 40 files
- Scratch scripts removed; backlog updated to mark the sweep DONE

That closes the **last** open item in the test-suite cleanup pass — the three slices you scoped (fetchMock fixture, `makeCategory` builder, and this tag/header sweep) are all done. `git status` shows 40 modified specs + the backlog, uncommitted for your review. I did not commit. (There's also an untracked `docs/SampleHierachy.txt` that isn't mine — left alone.)
Remaining tidy ups or refactorings?
Let me assess what's genuinely left rather than re-survey from scratch. Let me pull the open (non-DONE) items from the backlog and scan for the small residue the earlier analysis flagged.
